chunks: When Dharr ibn Abī Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, died, Abū Dharr stood by his grave, touched the grave with his hand, then said:

May Allah have mercy on you, O Dharr. By Allah, you were dutiful to me, and you have been taken while I am pleased with you. By Allah, your loss is not a humiliation for me, nor do I have any need of anyone besides Allah. Were it not for the terror of what is to be faced, it would have pleased me to be in your place. My grief for you has occupied me from grieving over you. By Allah, I did not weep for you, but rather I wept over you. Would that I knew what you said and what was said to you.

O Allah, I have gifted to him whatever right of mine You made obligatory upon him, so gift to him whatever right of Yours You made obligatory upon him, for You are worthier of generosity and nobility than I am.

key_terms.الْمُطَّلَعِ: the moment of exposure to the realities after death
key_terms.رَحِمَكَ: May Allah show mercy to you
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave; the burial place of the deceased
key_terms.هَوْلُ: terror or dread of a fearful matter
key_terms.وَهَبْتُ: I gave up or gifted freely

ai.seo_question: What did Abū Dharr say at the grave of his son, and what does it teach about grief and du'a for the deceased?
ai.summary: This report describes Abū Dharr’s grief at the grave of his son and his words of mercy, contentment, and surrender before Allah. It reflects awareness of the afterlife, the questioning after death, and the virtue of remitting one’s personal rights while asking Allah for pardon and generosity toward the deceased.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.558 - When Dhar ibn Abi Dhar, passed away, Abu Dharr stood by his grave, touched it with his hand, and said:
"May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, O’ Dhar. By Allah (swt), you were righteous toward me. You were taken from me while I am content with you. By Allah (swt), I have not felt your loss as a disgrace, nor have I sought from anyone besides Allah (swt) any need. Were it not for the terror of the grave and its trials, I would have been pleased to be in your place. Sorrow for you has preoccupied me from sorrow over your loss. By Allah (swt), I did not cry for you but for myself over you. I wonder what you said and what was said to you.
O’ Allah (swt), I have forgiven him what was due to me of rights. Grant him what is due from You, for You are more worthy of generosity and grace."
